key: In the next age they loved them and praised them. In the next they feared them; in the next they despised them.
s: The chapter says that in later ages they loved and praised them, then feared them, then despised them; Wang Bi, on chapter 17, takes these as lesser rulers: one who, unable to govern by non-action, sets up goodness and bestows favours, one who relies on power, and one who rules by cleverness and whose orders are evaded.
src: Wang Bi, Laozi zhu, chapter 17, zh.wikisource (the Huating Zhang edition), revision 2354026 (2024)

opened.edition: zh.wikisource 道德經 (王弼本), the 華亭張氏 edition, revision 2354026
opened.locator: chapter 17, comments on 其次，親而譽之 / 其次，畏之 / 其次，侮之

evidence.words: 不能以無為居事，不言為教，立善行施，使下得親而譽之也。…不復能以恩仁令物，而賴威權也。…不能法以正齊民，而以智治國，下知避之，其令不從
evidence.gloss: Unable to abide in affairs by non-action and to teach without words, he sets up goodness and dispenses favours, so that those below come to love and praise him. … No longer able to command things by kindness and benevolence, he relies on majesty and power. … Unable to order the people by correct law, he governs the state by cleverness; those below learn to evade him and his orders are not followed.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, ref Tao Te Ching 17, at [16]); two whole sentences in one unit. Wang Bi comments line by line on 其次親而譽之, 其次畏之, 其次侮之, and each of the three rulers in the sentence matches his comment (立善行施; 賴威權; 以智治國, 下知避之, 其令不從). 'Lesser' is fair for his 其次 set against the 大人 of the first line. 'Whose orders are evaded' compresses 下知避之，其令不從 without adding to it. Plain sense faithful. entry-check ok.
